sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca na praṇāśo 'sti jīvānāṃ dattasya ca kṛtasya ca yāti dehāntaraṃ prāṇī śarīraṃ tu viśīryate
english: Bhṛgu said: There is no perishing for living beings, nor for what is given and what is done. The living creature passes into another body, while only the body wastes away.

sanskrit: na śarīrāśrito jīvas tasmin naṣṭe praṇaśyati yathā samitsu dagdhāsu na praṇaśyati pāvakaḥ
english: The living soul, though housed in the body, does not perish when the body is destroyed—just as fire does not perish when the firewood is burnt up.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca agner yathā tathā tasya yadi nāśo na vidyate indhanasyopayogānte sa cāgnir nopalabhyate
english: Bharadvāja said: If the soul knows no destruction, just as fire does not, then why, when the fuel has been wholly consumed, is that fire no longer to be found?

sanskrit: naśyatīty eva jānāmi śāntam agnim anindhanam gatir yasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na dṛśyate
english: I take it that a fire grown quiet for want of fuel has perished, for neither its course, nor its measure, nor its abiding form can any longer be seen.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca samidhām upayogānte sann evāgnir na dṛśyate ākāśānugatatvād dhi durgrahaḥ sa nirāśrayaḥ
english: Bhṛgu said: When the fuel is spent, the fire, though still existing, is not seen; for, having passed into the ether and being without support, it is hard to grasp.

sanskrit: tathā śarīrasaṃtyāge jīvo hy ākāśavat sthitaḥ na gṛhyate susūkṣmatvād yathā jyotir na saṃśayaḥ
english: So too, when the body is forsaken, the soul abides like the ether and cannot be grasped, by reason of its extreme subtlety—exactly as the fire is not grasped. Of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: prāṇān dhārayate hy agniḥ sa jīva upadhāryatām vāyusaṃdhāraṇo hy agnir naśyaty ucchvāsanigrahāt
english: It is fire that upholds the vital breaths; know that fire to be the living soul. Sustained by the breath, that fire is extinguished when respiration is checked.

sanskrit: tasmin naṣṭe śarīrāgnau śarīraṃ tad acetanam patitaṃ yāti bhūmitvam ayanaṃ tasya hi kṣitiḥ
english: When that bodily fire is extinguished, the body, now bereft of consciousness, falls and returns to the state of earth; for earth is its final resting place.

sanskrit: jaṅgamānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ākāśaṃ pavano 'bhyeti jyotis tam anugacchati tatra trayāṇām ekatvaṃ dvayaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhitam
english: In all things that move and likewise in all that are fixed, the wind merges into the ether and the fire follows after it. Therein lies the oneness of these three, while the remaining two are established in the earth.

sanskrit: yatra khaṃ tatra pavanas tatrāgnir yatra mārutaḥ amūrtayas te vijñeyā āpo mūrtās tathā kṣitiḥ
english: Where there is space, there is wind; where there is wind, there is fire. These are to be understood as formless, whereas water and earth possess form.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca yady agnimārutau bhūmiḥ kham āpaś ca śarīriṣu jīvaḥ kiṃlakṣaṇas tatrety etad ācakṣva me 'nagha
english: Bharadvāja said: If fire and wind, earth, ether, and water are present in embodied beings, then what are the marks of the soul within them? Declare this to me, O sinless one.

sanskrit: pañcātmake pañcaratau pañcavijñānasaṃyute śarīre prāṇināṃ jīvaṃ jñātum icchāmi yādṛśam
english: The body of living beings is made of the five elements, delights in the five objects, and is joined with the five forms of perception. Of what nature is the soul within it? This I wish to know.

sanskrit: māṃsaśoṇitasaṃghāte medaḥsnāyvasthisaṃcaye bhidyamāne śarīre tu jīvo naivopalabhyate
english: When the body—a compound of flesh and blood, a heap of fat, sinew, and bone—is cleft open, the soul is nowhere to be found within it.

sanskrit: yady ajīvaṃ śarīraṃ tu pañcabhūtasamanvitam śārīre mānase duḥkhe kas tāṃ vedayate rujam
english: If the body, though endowed with the five elements, is itself without a soul, then who is it that feels the pang, whether the pain be bodily or of the mind?

sanskrit: śṛṇoti kathitaṃ jīvaḥ karṇābhyāṃ na śṛṇoti tat maharṣe manasi vyagre tasmāj jīvo nirarthakaḥ
english: It is the soul that hears what is spoken; the ears do not hear it of themselves—for when the mind is distracted, nothing is heard. Hence, O great seer, the soul would seem to serve no purpose.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ paśyati yad dṛśyaṃ manoyuktena cakṣuṣā manasi vyākule tad dhi paśyann api na paśyati
english: With the eye joined to the mind one sees all that is to be seen; but when the mind is troubled, one looks yet does not truly see.

sanskrit: na paśyati na ca brūte na śṛṇoti na jighrati na ca sparśarasau vetti nidrāvaśagataḥ punaḥ
english: Again, one overcome by sleep neither sees nor speaks, neither hears nor smells, nor knows touch and taste.

sanskrit: hṛṣyati krudhyati ca kaḥ śocaty udvijate ca kaḥ icchati dhyāyati dveṣṭi vācam īrayate ca kaḥ
english: Who is it that rejoices and grows angry, that grieves and is dismayed? Who is it that desires, reflects, and hates, and who is it that utters speech?

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca na pañcasādhāraṇam atra kiṃ cic; charīram eko vahate 'ntarātmā sa vetti gandhāṃś ca rasāñ śrutiṃ ca; sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca guṇāś ca ye 'nye
english: Bhṛgu said: Here nothing belongs in common to the five elements; the inner Self alone, being one, bears the body. It it is that knows smells and tastes and sound, and touch and form, and whatever other qualities there are.

sanskrit: pañcātmake pañcaguṇapradarśī; sa sarvagātrānugato 'ntarātmā sa vetti duḥkhāni sukhāni cātra; tadviprayogāt tu na vetti dehaḥ
english: Within the fivefold frame, perceiving the five qualities and pervading every limb, dwells the inner Self. It it is that knows the pains and pleasures here; but once parted from it, the body knows nothing.

sanskrit: yadā na rūpaṃ na sparśo noṣmabhāvaś ca pāvake tadā śānte śarīrāgnau dehaṃ tyaktvā sa naśyati
english: When the fire has neither form nor touch nor the quality of warmth, then, the bodily fire being quenched, the Self forsakes the body and passes from sight.

sanskrit: ammayaṃ sarvam evedam āpo mūrtiḥ śarīriṇām tatrātmā mānaso brahmā sarvabhūteṣu lokakṛt
english: All this is made of water; water is the very substance of embodied beings. Therein dwells the Self—Brahmā born of mind, the world-maker present in all creatures.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ taṃ vijānīhi sarvalokahitātmakam tasmin yaḥ saṃśrito dehe hy abbindur iva puṣkare
english: Know that Self to be the very ground of the welfare of all the worlds—the one who dwells within this body as a drop of water rests upon a lotus leaf.

sanskrit: kṣetrajñaṃ taṃ vijānīhi nityaṃ lokahitātmakam tamo rajaś ca sattvaṃ ca viddhi jīvaguṇān imān
english: Know him to be the Knower of the Field, ever devoted to the good of the world; and know these—darkness (tamas), passion (rajas), and goodness (sattva)—to be the qualities of the living soul.

sanskrit: sacetanaṃ jīvaguṇaṃ vadanti; sa ceṣṭate ceṣṭayate ca sarvam tataḥ paraṃ kṣetravidaṃ vadanti; prāvartayad yo bhuvanāni sapta
english: The wise call consciousness a quality of the soul; it acts and sets all things in motion. Beyond it they speak of the Knower of the Field—he who set in motion the seven worlds.

sanskrit: na jīvanāśo 'sti hi dehabhede; mithyaitad āhur mṛta ity abuddhāḥ jīvas tu dehāntaritaḥ prayāti; daśārdhataivāsya śarīrabhedaḥ
english: There is no destruction of the soul when the body is sundered; falsely do the unknowing call a man dead. The soul, passing into another body, journeys on; the breaking of the body is but the dispersal of its five elements.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhaś carati saṃvṛtaḥ dṛśyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā tattvadarśibhiḥ
english: Thus, hidden and enveloped, the soul moves within all beings; yet by the foremost, subtle intellect it is beheld by those who perceive the truth.

sanskrit: taṃ pūrvāpararātreṣu yuñjānaḥ satataṃ budhaḥ laghvāhāro viśuddhātmā paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: The wise man who, in the first and last watches of the night, ever yokes himself in concentration, eating but little and pure in soul, beholds the Self within the self.

sanskrit: cittasya hi prasādena hitvā karma śubhāśubham prasannātmātmani sthitvā sukham akṣayam aśnute
english: For through the serenity of his mind, having abandoned action both good and evil, the man of tranquil soul, abiding in the Self, attains imperishable bliss.

sanskrit: mānaso 'gniḥ śarīreṣu jīva ity abhidhīyate sṛṣṭiḥ prajāpater eṣā bhūtādhyātmaviniścaye
english: The fire born of mind within bodies is what is called the living soul. Such is the creation of Prajāpati, set forth in this inquiry into the elements and the Self.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca asṛjad brāhmaṇān eva pūrvaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ ātmatejobhinirvṛttān bhāskarāgnisamaprabhān
english: Bhṛgu said: First of all, Brahmā the Lord of creatures brought forth the brāhmaṇas alone, fashioned from his own radiance and shining like the sun and fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca tapo brahma ca śāśvatam ācāraṃ caiva śaucaṃ ca svargāya vidadhe prabhuḥ
english: Then the Lord ordained, for the sake of heaven, truth and dharma, austerity and the eternal sacred lore, right conduct, and purity.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvadaityāsuramahoragāḥ yakṣarākṣasanāgāś ca piśācā manujās tathā
english: The gods, dānavas, gandharvas, daityas, asuras, and great serpents; the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and nāgas; the piśācas, and likewise human beings;

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś ca dvijasattama ye cānye bhūtasaṃghānāṃ saṃghās tāṃś cāpi nirmame
english: the brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, O best of the twice-born, and whatever other hosts among the multitudes of beings there are—all these too he fashioned.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ sito varṇaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu lohitaḥ vaiśyānāṃ pītako varṇaḥ śūdrāṇām asitas tathā
english: White was the color of the brāhmaṇas, red that of the kṣatriyas, yellow the color of the vaiśyas, and black that of the śūdras.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca cāturvarṇyasya varṇena yadi varṇo vibhajyate sarveṣāṃ khalu varṇānāṃ dṛśyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: If the four orders are to be distinguished by color, then surely among all the orders a mingling of colors is to be seen.

sanskrit: kāmaḥ krodho bhayaṃ lobhaḥ śokaś cintā kṣudhā śramaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ prabhavati kasmād varṇo vibhajyate
english: Desire, anger, fear, greed, grief, anxiety, hunger, and weariness arise in all of us alike; by what mark, then, is the order distinguished?

sanskrit: svedamūtrapurīṣāṇi śleṣmā pittaṃ saśoṇitam tanuḥ kṣarati sarveṣāṃ kasmād varṇo vibhajyate
english: Sweat, urine, and dung, phlegm, bile, and blood—the body of every man oozes with these; by what, then, is the order distinguished?

sanskrit: jaṅgamānām asaṃkhyeyāḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jātayaḥ teṣāṃ vividhavarṇānāṃ kuto varṇaviniścayaḥ
english: Countless are the kinds of moving creatures and of fixed; among these, of so many varied colors, whence comes any fixed determination of order?

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca na viśeṣo 'sti varṇānāṃ sarvaṃ brāhmam idaṃ jagat brahmaṇā pūrvasṛṣṭaṃ hi karmabhir varṇatāṃ gatam
english: Bhṛgu said: There is in truth no distinction among the orders; this whole world is Brahman. Created of old by Brahmā, it came through deeds to its division into orders.

sanskrit: kāmabhogapriyās tīkṣṇāḥ krodhanāḥ priyasāhasāḥ tyaktasvadharmā raktāṅgās te dvijāḥ kṣatratāṃ gatāḥ
english: Those twice-born who, loving desire and pleasure, fierce, prone to wrath, and delighting in bold deeds, forsook their own dharma and turned ruddy of limb—these passed into the state of kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: goṣu vṛttiṃ samādhāya pītāḥ kṛṣyupajīvinaḥ svadharmaṃ nānutiṣṭhanti te dvijā vaiśyatāṃ gatāḥ
english: Those who, taking up a livelihood among cattle and living by the plow, turned yellow and did not keep to their own dharma—these twice-born passed into the state of vaiśyas.

sanskrit: hiṃsānṛtapriyā lubdhāḥ sarvakarmopajīvinaḥ kṛṣṇāḥ śaucaparibhraṣṭās te dvijāḥ śūdratāṃ gatāḥ
english: Those who, loving violence and falsehood, greedy, living by every kind of work, turned black and fell from purity—these twice-born passed into the state of śūdras.

sanskrit: ity etaiḥ karmabhir vyastā dvijā varṇāntaraṃ gatāḥ dharmo yajñakriyā caiṣāṃ nityaṃ na pratiṣidhyate
english: Thus, sundered by these several deeds, the twice-born passed into other orders; yet dharma and the performance of sacrifice are never forbidden them.

sanskrit: varṇāś catvāra ete hi yeṣāṃ brāhmī sarasvatī vihitā brahmaṇā pūrvaṃ lobhāt tv ajñānatāṃ gatāḥ
english: These four orders, for whom the sacred speech of Brahman was ordained by Brahmā of old, through greed fell into a state of ignorance.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā dharmatantrasthās tapas teṣāṃ na naśyati brahma dhārayatāṃ nityaṃ vratāni niyamāṃs tathā
english: The brāhmaṇas who abide in the discipline of dharma—their austerity does not perish, for they ever uphold the sacred lore, the vows, and the restraints.

sanskrit: brahma caitat purā sṛṣṭaṃ ye na jānanty atadvidaḥ teṣāṃ bahuvidhās tv anyās tatra tatra hi jātayaḥ
english: This sacred lore was brought forth of old, yet those who do not know it, being unlearned in it—from them arise, here and there, manifold other kinds of beings.

sanskrit: piśācā rākṣasāḥ pretā bahudhā mlecchajātayaḥ pranaṣṭajñānavijñānāḥ svacchandācāraceṣṭitāḥ
english: Piśācas, rākṣasas, and pretas, and the barbarian races in their many forms—their knowledge and discernment lost, given over to conduct and pursuits of their own willful choosing.

sanskrit: prajā brāhmaṇasaṃskārāḥ svadharmakṛtaniścayāḥ ṛṣibhiḥ svena tapasā sṛjyante cāpare paraiḥ
english: Those creatures who bear the consecrations of the brāhmaṇas and are resolved upon their own dharma are brought forth by the seers through their own austerity, while others again are created by other beings.

sanskrit: ādidevasamudbhūtā brahmamūlākṣayāvyayā sā sṛṣṭir mānasī nāma dharmatantraparāyaṇā
english: Sprung from the First God, rooted in Brahman, imperishable and undecaying—that creation is called the mind-born, wholly devoted to the discipline of dharma.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca brāhmaṇaḥ kena bhavati kṣatriyo vā dvijottama vaiśyaḥ śūdraś ca viprarṣe tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara
english: Bharadvāja said: By what does one become a brāhmaṇa, or a kṣatriya, O best of the twice-born, or a vaiśya, or a śūdra, O brāhmaṇa-sage? Declare this, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca jātakarmādibhir yas tu saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ śuciḥ vedādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ ṣaṭsu karmasv avasthitaḥ
english: Bhṛgu said: He who is consecrated and purified by the rites that begin with the birth-ceremony, accomplished in the study of the Veda, and established in the six duties;

sanskrit: śaucācārasthitaḥ samyag vighasāśī gurupriyaḥ nityavratī satyaparaḥ sa vai brāhmaṇa ucyate
english: who stands firm in purity and right conduct, eats only what remains after offering, holds his teacher dear, is constant in his vows, and devoted to truth—he indeed is called a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: satyaṃ dānaṃ damo 'droha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṣamā ghṛṇā tapaś ca dṛśyate yatra sa brāhmaṇa iti smṛtaḥ
english: In whom are seen truth, charity, self-restraint, freedom from malice, kindliness, forbearance, compassion, and austerity—he is remembered as a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṣatrajaṃ sevate karma vedādhyayanasaṃmataḥ dānādānaratir yaś ca sa vai kṣatriya ucyate
english: He who follows the work befitting a kṣatriya, is devoted to the study of the Veda, and takes delight in giving and receiving—he indeed is called a kṣatriya.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ yo viśaty aniśaṃ śuciḥ vedādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ sa vaiśya iti saṃjñitaḥ
english: He who, pure, devotes himself unceasingly to farming, the tending of cattle, and trade, and is accomplished in the study of the Veda—he is named a vaiśya.

sanskrit: sarvabhakṣaratir nityaṃ sarvakarmakaro 'śuciḥ tyaktavedas tv anācāraḥ sa vai śūdra iti smṛtaḥ
english: He who takes pleasure in eating all things, does every kind of work, is impure, has forsaken the Veda, and is without right conduct—he indeed is remembered as a śūdra.

sanskrit: śūdre caitad bhavel lakṣyaṃ dvije caitan na vidyate na vai śūdro bhavec chūdro brāhmaṇo na ca brāhmaṇaḥ
english: If this mark be found in a śūdra and be lacking in one twice-born, then in truth the śūdra is no śūdra, nor is the brāhmaṇa a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: sarvopāyais tu lobhasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ etat pavitraṃ jñātavyaṃ tathā caivātmasaṃyamaḥ
english: The curbing of greed and of anger by every means—this is to be known as the true purifier, and likewise the mastery of oneself.

sanskrit: nityaṃ krodhāt tapo rakṣec chriyaṃ rakṣeta matsarāt vidyāṃ mānāvamānābhyām ātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ
english: One should ever guard one's austerity from anger, one's prosperity from envy, one's learning from honor and dishonor alike, and one's very self from heedlessness.

sanskrit: yasya sarve samārambhā nirāśīrbandhanās tv iha tyāge yasya hutaṃ sarvaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān
english: He whose every undertaking here is free from the bond of craving, and who has offered up everything in renunciation—he is the true renouncer, and he alone is wise.

sanskrit: ahiṃsraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ maitrāyaṇagataś caret avisrambhe na gantavyaṃ visrambhe dhārayen manaḥ
english: Doing harm to no living being, let him walk in the way of friendliness toward all. Where there is no trust one should not go; where there is trust, let him fix his mind.

sanskrit: parigrahān parityajya bhaved buddhyā jitendriyaḥ aśokaṃ sthānam ātiṣṭhed iha cāmutra cābhayam
english: Casting off all possessions, let him through wisdom subdue his senses; thus he shall attain that sorrowless state, free from fear both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: taponityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmanā ajitaṃ jetukāmena bhāvyaṃ saṅgeṣv asaṅginā
english: The sage who is constant in austerity, self-controlled and self-restrained, desiring to conquer what is yet unconquered, must remain unattached amid all attachments.

sanskrit: indriyair gṛhyate yad yat tat tad vyaktam iti sthitiḥ avyaktam iti vijñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyam atīndriyam
english: Whatever is grasped by the senses—that is the manifest; such is the settled truth. But that which lies beyond the senses, to be apprehended only by inference through its marks, is to be known as the unmanifest.

sanskrit: manaḥ prāṇe nigṛhṇīyāt prāṇaṃ brahmaṇi dhārayet nirvāṇād eva nirvāṇo na ca kiṃ cid vicintayet sukhaṃ vai brāhmaṇo brahma sa vai tenādhigacchati
english: Let him restrain the mind within the breath and hold the breath fixed in Brahman; passing from extinction into extinction itself, let him think upon nothing whatsoever. Brahman is bliss for the brāhmaṇa, and thereby indeed he attains it.

sanskrit: śaucena satataṃ yuktas tathācārasamanvitaḥ sānukrośaś ca bhūteṣu tad dvijātiṣu lakṣaṇam
english: Ever joined to purity, endowed with right conduct, and full of compassion toward all beings—such is the mark of the twice-born.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca satyaṃ brahma tapaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ sṛjati ca prajāḥ satyena dhāryate lokaḥ svargaṃ satyena gacchati
english: Bhṛgu said: Truth is Brahman, truth is austerity; truth it is that brings forth all creatures. By truth the world is upheld, and by truth one goes to heaven.

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ tamaso rūpaṃ tamasā nīyate hy adhaḥ tamograstā na paśyanti prakāśaṃ tamasāvṛtam
english: Falsehood is the very form of darkness, and by darkness a man is led downward. Those seized by darkness do not behold the light, for it is veiled by darkness.

sanskrit: svargaḥ prakāśa ity āhur narakaṃ tama eva ca satyānṛtāt tad ubhayaṃ prāpyate jagatīcaraiḥ
english: Heaven, they say, is light, and hell is darkness; both of these are reached by the wayfarers of the world according to their truth and falsehood.

sanskrit: tatra tv evaṃvidhā vṛttir loke satyānṛtā bhavet dharmādharmau prakāśaś ca tamo duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ tathā
english: In this world, then, the manner of life is of this twofold kind, mingled of truth and falsehood—dharma and its opposite, light and darkness, sorrow and likewise joy.

sanskrit: tatra yat satyaṃ sa dharmo yo dharmaḥ sa prakāśo yaḥ prakāśas tat sukham iti tatra yad anṛtaṃ so 'dharmo yo 'dharmas tat tamo yat tamas tad duḥkham iti
english: Therein, what is truth is dharma; what is dharma is light; what is light is joy. And therein, what is falsehood is unrighteousness; what is unrighteousness is darkness; what is darkness is sorrow.

sanskrit: śārīrair mānasair duḥkhaiḥ sukhaiś cāpy asukhodayaiḥ atrocyate lokasṛṣṭiṃ prapaśyanto na muhyanti vicakṣaṇāḥ
english: Of the pains, bodily and mental, and of the pleasures whose end is yet pain, it is here spoken; and the discerning, beholding the creation of the world, are not deluded.

sanskrit: tatra duḥkhavimokṣārthaṃ prayateta vicakṣaṇaḥ sukhaṃ hy anityaṃ bhūtānām iha loke paratra ca
english: Therefore let the discerning man strive for release from sorrow; for the happiness of beings is fleeting, both in this world and in the next.

sanskrit: rāhugrastasya somasya yathā jyotsnā na bhāsate tathā tamobhibhūtānāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhraśyate sukham
english: As the moonlight of the moon seized by Rāhu no longer shines, so for beings overwhelmed by darkness all happiness slips away.

sanskrit: tat khalu dvividhaṃ sukham ucyate śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ca iha khalv amuṣmiṃś ca loke sarvārambhapravṛttayaḥ sukhārthā abhidhīyante na hy atas trivargaphalaṃ viśiṣṭataram asti sa eṣa kāmyo guṇaviśeṣo dharmārthayor ārambhas taddhetur asyotpattiḥ sukhaprayojanā
english: That happiness, then, is said to be of two kinds—bodily and mental. Here and in the world beyond, all undertakings and exertions are declared to have happiness for their aim; for there is no fruit of the threefold ends of life more excellent than this. This is the desirable, the supreme good; the undertaking of dharma and of wealth is its cause, and its arising has happiness for its purpose.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca yad etad bhavatābhihitaṃ sukhānāṃ paramāḥ striya iti tan na gṛhṇīmaḥ na hy eṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ mahati sthitānām aprāpya eṣa guṇaviśeṣo na cainam abhilaṣanti śrūyate ca bhagavāṃs trilokakṛd brahmā prabhur ekākī tiṣṭhati brahmacārī na kāmasukheṣv ātmānam avadadhāti api ca bhagavān viśveśvara umāpatiḥ kāmam abhivartamānam anaṅgatvena śamam anayat tasmād brūmo na mahātmabhir ayaṃ pratigṛhīto na tv eṣa tāvad viśiṣṭo guṇa iti naitad bhagavataḥ pratyemi bhagavatā tūktaṃ sukhānāṃ paramāḥ striya iti
english: Bharadvāja said: As for what you have declared—that women are the highest of pleasures—this we do not accept. For to these seers, established in greatness, this supreme good is not beyond reach, and yet they do not crave it. It is heard, moreover, that the Lord Brahmā, maker of the three worlds, abides alone, chaste, and does not give himself over to the pleasures of desire. And the Lord Umā's consort, the Sovereign of the universe, when Desire assailed him, brought him to quietude by rendering him bodiless. Therefore we say that this is not embraced by the great-souled, and that it is not, after all, so excellent a good. I cannot accept this from your honored self, though your honor has indeed said that women are the highest of pleasures.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca anṛtāt khalu tamaḥ prādurbhūtaṃ tamograstā adharmam evānuvartante na dharmam krodhalobhamohamānānṛtādibhir avacchannā na khalv asmiṃl loke na cāmutra sukham āpnuvanti vividhavyādhigaṇopatāpair avakīryante vadhabandharogaparikleśādibhiś ca kṣutpipāsāśramakṛtair upatāpair upatapyante caṇḍavātātyuṣṇātiśītakṛtaiś ca pratibhayaiḥ śārīrair duḥkhair upatapyante bandhudhanavināśaviprayogakṛtaiś ca mānasaiḥ śokair abhibhūyante jarāmṛtyukṛtaiś cānyair iti
english: Bhṛgu said: From falsehood, indeed, darkness arose; those seized by darkness follow after unrighteousness alone, and not dharma. Enveloped by anger, greed, delusion, pride, falsehood, and the like, they win no happiness, neither in this world nor in the next. They are strewn over by the torments of manifold diseases, and afflicted by killing, bondage, sickness, distress, and the like; they are tormented by the pains born of hunger, thirst, and weariness, and by the terrors born of fierce winds, excessive heat, and bitter cold. By bodily pains they are tormented, and by mental griefs born of the destruction and loss of kin and wealth, and by yet others born of old age and death, they are overcome.

sanskrit: yas tv etaiḥ śārīrair mānasair duḥkhair na spṛśyate sa sukhaṃ veda na caite doṣāḥ svarge prādurbhavanti tatra bhavati khalu
english: But he who is untouched by these pains, bodily and mental, knows true happiness. These ills do not arise in heaven; there, indeed, it comes to pass that—

sanskrit: susukhaḥ pavanaḥ svarge gandhaś ca surabhis tathā kṣutpipāsāśramo nāsti na jarā na ca pāpakam
english: in heaven the breeze blows full of ease and the fragrance is sweet; there is no hunger, thirst, or weariness, no old age, and nothing evil.
